proposal.contractText:
Owner: project-2-claude writes shared/cards.js. project-2-droid imports it; does NOT produce its own version.

File: shared/cards.js
Format: CommonJS (module.exports = {...}); no Node-only built-ins in module scope so the file is also loadable in-browser as window.Cards via a <script> tag.

Exported constants:
  COLUMNS: ['todo', 'in-progress', 'done']   // canonical order
  TITLE_MAX: 80

Exported functions:

  newId() -> string
    Returns a UUID v4 string via crypto.randomUUID().

  validateCard(input, options) -> {ok: true, value: NormalizedCard} | {ok: false, errors: string[], fields: {title?:string, description?:string, assignee?:string, column?:string, position?:string}}
    options: {partial?: boolean}  // if partial=true, title is not required (for PATCH updates)
    Normalization rules:
      title: string, trimmed; required unless partial=true; length 1–80 chars after trim
      description: string, trimmed; defaults to '' if absent or null
      assignee: string, trimmed; defaults to '' if absent or null
      column: must be one of COLUMNS; defaults to 'todo' if absent on a non-partial call
      position: integer >= 0 (only validated when present)
    On failure: ok=false, errors=[...human strings], fields={fieldName: firstErrorForField}
    On success: ok=true, value=normalized card object (with defaults applied)

NormalizedCard shape (output of validateCard .value):
  {title:string, description:string, assignee:string, column:string, position?:number}
  (id and position may be absent from validation output; server assigns id via newId() and position via store)

Browser usage: <script src="/shared/cards.js"></script> exposes window.Cards = {COLUMNS, TITLE_MAX, newId, validateCard}.
proposal.rationale: Both Claude (item 5) and Droid (item 8) plan to produce shared/cards.js. Droid explicitly offers to cede ownership to Claude. Claude is named owner here. Droid must NOT write shared/cards.js and must import it instead. Key conflicts to resolve: column list ('doing' from Claude vs 'in-progress' from Droid) — 'in-progress' wins because it is used in store keys by the store owner (Droid). Function signatures reconciled: validateCard uses Claude's {partial} option shape but must return {ok,value/errors} (not throw), so the server can produce the per-field error body required by Codex (item 14). Droid's createId()/newId() name is standardized to newId() (Claude's name). description and assignee default to '' per Droid's spec.

Claude (producer, item 3) and Droid (item 9) agree on card fields and REST routes, but Codex (item 11) assumes a different route set (GET /api/board, POST /api/cards/:id/move instead of PATCH /api/cards/:id), different column IDs (backlog, in_progress, review, done vs todo, in-progress, done), and a different move mechanism. Because Claude owns the server and Droid defers to agreement, the contract adopts Claude's routes and card shape. Codex stated it is flexible to the teammate contract. Column IDs are pinned to todo, in-progress, done (reconciling Claude's todo/doing/done with Droid's todo/in-progress/done — 'in-progress' wins because Droid is the store owner and uses it in storage keys; 'doing' from Claude is renamed to 'in-progress'). proposal.contractText:
Transport: Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Stream endpoint:
  GET /api/events
  Response headers: Content-Type: text/event-stream; Cache-Control: no-cache; Connection: keep-alive
  HTTP 200, connection held open indefinitely.

Heartbeat (keep-alive): server writes `: ping\n\n` every 25 seconds.

Event format (each change):
  event: <event-name>\n
  data: <JSON>\n\n

Event names and data payloads:
  card.created  — data: full Card JSON of the created card
  card.updated  — data: full Card JSON of the updated card
  card.moved    — data: full Card JSON of the moved card (with new column and position); clients MUST refetch GET /api/cards to observe all reindexed sibling positions
  card.deleted  — data: full Card JSON of the deleted card (as it was before deletion)

Card JSON shape in all event data payloads:
{"id":string, "title":string, "description":string, "assignee":string, "column":string, "position":integer}

Reconnect behavior: browser EventSource reconnects automatically on connection drop; server sends no Last-Event-ID replay (clients refetch GET /api/cards on reconnect to resync).

Store's internal change event (emitted by store/index.js after durable write, consumed only by server/index.js):
  emitter.on('change', {type: string, card: Card})
  type values: 'card.created' | 'card.updated' | 'card.moved' | 'card.deleted'
  (No 'board' field in the internal envelope; server fans out to SSE clients directly from {type,card}.)
proposal.rationale: Claude (producer, item 4) uses SSE (text/event-stream) over GET /api/events. Codex (item 12) initially assumes WebSocket /ws with full board JSON, but explicitly states it is flexible to EventSource /api/events with named events and a refetch pattern. Droid (item 10) defers transport to Claude and will adapt its store change envelope. The conflict is resolved by adopting Claude's SSE design. The key pinnable details Codex requires (stream payload, reconnect behavior) are spelled out. Droid's proposed {type,card,board} envelope is adapted: the SSE 'data' field carries only the card JSON (not the full board), matching Claude's spec; clients that want full board state after card.moved refetch GET /api/cards. Heartbeat and reconnect behavior are pinned.

proposal.contractText:
File: store/index.js
Format: CommonJS (module.exports = createStore)
Owner: project-2-droid

Factory:
  createStore({filePath: string}) -> Promise<store>
  (filePath is the path to the JSON persistence file; created if absent)

Returned store object — all methods are async (return Promises):

  getBoard() -> Promise<{cards: Card[]}>
    Returns all cards in an object. cards array order is unspecified (server sorts).

  createCard(input: {id:string, title:string, description:string, assignee:string, column:string, position:integer}) -> Promise<Card>
    Server supplies id (via newId()), validated fields, and position (end of column).
    Persists and emits change event.

  updateCard(id: string, patch: {title?:string, description?:string, assignee?:string}) -> Promise<Card>
    Applies patch to existing card. Throws statusCode=404 Error if not found.
    Persists and emits change event.

  moveCard(id: string, {column: string, position: integer}) -> Promise<Card>
    Moves card to column at 0-based position. Reindexes positions in source column (fills gap) and target column (inserts, shifts up). Returns updated card.
    Throws statusCode=404 Error if not found, statusCode=400 if column invalid.
    Persists and emits change event.

  deleteCard(id: string) -> Promise<Card>
    Removes card, reindexes remaining cards in that column. Returns the deleted Card.
    Throws statusCode=404 Error if not found.
    Persists and emits change event.

Card shape stored and returned:
  {id:string, title:string, description:string, assignee:string, column:string, position:integer}
  Positions are 0-based integers, contiguous within each column, after every mutating operation.

Change events (EventEmitter):
  store.on('change', ({type: string, card: Card}) => ...)
  type values: 'card.created' | 'card.updated' | 'card.moved' | 'card.deleted'
  Emitted only after the durable write completes.

Error protocol:
  Not-found: throw Object.assign(new Error('Not found'), {statusCode: 404})
  Validation: throw Object.assign(new Error('...'), {statusCode: 400})

Canonical columns (in order): ['todo', 'in-progress', 'done']
Server (Claude) must call Droid's method names above; server does NOT call list/get/create/update/move/remove.
proposal.rationale: Droid owns and produces store/index.js (item 7); Claude's server depends on it (item 6); Codex requires the API and store agree on column IDs and position model (item 13). The main tension is method naming: Claude's server was written expecting list/get/create/update/move/remove, while Droid plans getBoard/createCard/updateCard/moveCard/deleteCard. Because both sides need to build in parallel, the contract pins the exact exported method names and signatures. Droid's async EventEmitter 'change' event is adopted. The contract chooses Droid's method names (as store owner) and requires Claude's server to call those names. Column IDs and position model are pinned to the board.api contract values.
